comments.author: ppwwyyxx
comments.body: thanks, this is a bug. However the device for `PolygonMasks` should always be `torch.device('cpu')` so you can use it instead.

comments.author: TengFeiHan0
comments.body:
@ppwwyyxx  I'm so sorry to trouble you again and leave a comment on a closed issue. 
why the device for `PolygonMasks` should always be `torch.device('cpu')`? if possible, could you give me some cues? if `PolygonMasks` is not a tensor, the following operations, such as `permute()`, `mask.shape`, become meaningless.  how to solve the new arising problem? probably `BitMasks` is an alternative for `PolygonMasks`?

comments.author: ppwwyyxx
comments.body: `.device` is just to provide a similar interface to tensor/BitMasks - although it's not a tensor - so that the same code that uses `.device` can work on all three common types of mask representation.

comments.author: TengFeiHan0
comments.body:
@ppwwyyxx 
if `mask `is an object of PolygonMasks, what I want to do is acquire its shape, like `n, h, w = mask.shape`  then I got an error `'PolygonMasks' object has no attribute 'shape'`, which means shape operation for  `PolygonMasks `is prohibited. So where am I wrong? thank you in advance.

comments.author: ppwwyyxx
comments.body:
There is no `shape` attribute.
If you want to get the BitMask representation of a PolygonMask, you need https://detectron2.readthedocs.io/modules/structures.html#detectron2.structures.BitMasks.from_polygon_masks
